content: Indication-specific dosing for the combination of aetheroleum, balm mint, black peppermint, and peppermint oil involves the following: Dosage and Administration: Use 2 mL of the preparation diluted in 2 mL of isotonic saline. Apply topically as needed (PRN) every 15 to 30 minutes. Indications: This combination is possibly effective for the management of colic, common cold, dysmenorrhea, indigestion, inflammation of the mouth or pharynx, irritable bowel syndrome, nausea/vomiting, pain, respiratory infections, and tension headaches. Adverse Effects: General Adverse Effects: Allergic reactions, burning mouth syndrome, diarrhea, flushing, headache, heartburn, and mouth ulcers. Adverse Effects from Topical Use: Bronchospasm (notably in pediatric patients), contact dermatitis, laryngospasm (notably in pediatric patients), respiratory collapse, and skin irritation. Adverse Effects from Overdose: Acute renal failure, interstitial nephritis, and achlorhydria (associated with enteric-coated capsules). Contraindications: Avoid use in individuals with hiatal hernia. Avoid use during pregnancy and lactation. Pregnancy and Lactation: Pregnancy Category: Avoid use. Lactation: Avoid use. Category A: Generally acceptable. Controlled studies in pregnant women show no evidence of fetal risk. Pharmacokinetics: Metabolism: Not available (N/A). Excretion: Not available (N/A). Active Components and Mechanism of Action: Menthol, flavonoids, and azulene exhibit spasmolytic (antispasmodic) and stimulatory properties.
